question: Which of the following most often causes cholestatic jaundice:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Erythromycin estolate" -> "inhibits bile flow" -> "accumulation of bile in the liver" -> "cholestatic jaundice" -> 75%
CHAIN: "INH" -> "mild liver enzyme elevation" -> "rarely leads to cholestasis" -> "unlikely cause of cholestatic jaundice" -> 30%
CHAIN: "Pyrazinamide" -> "can cause liver injury" -> "more often hepatocellular than cholestatic" -> "less likely cause of cholestatic jaundice" -> 40%
CHAIN: "Ethionamide" -> "hepatotoxic effects" -> "primarily hepatocellular damage" -> "infrequent cause of cholestatic jaundice" -> 35%
analysis: Erythromycin estolate is the most likely among the options to cause cholestatic jaundice, supported by its known mechanism of action on bile flow and clinical evidence of its hepatotoxic profile. Other options, while hepatotoxic, generally cause hepatocellular damage rather than cholestasis.
